The front-expiry straddle implies about 11.3% (10.1% for the event after ordinary vol). The 25-delta skew is +23.9 vol points, so downside protection is bid, but the chain is thin: 1,192 contracts of open interest and an ATM spread of 57% of mid. September-quarter consensus sits at the guide: $375-377M revenue and $1.43-1.44 non-GAAP EPS (guide $375M +/- $20M, $1.42 +/- 10%). The Earnings Whispers whisper is $1.61. view: The September quarter will almost certainly beat. Management has beaten the top of its range recently: Q3 revenue was $330.4M against a $290-330M guide, and non-GAAP EPS was $1.20 against about $1.00. OSAT demand was still rising in October: ASE's ATM revenue was +7.9% month on month and +57.7% year on year. ASMPT reported record Q3 bookings with TCB at an all-time high. The line the stock trades on is the December guide plus the second-half FY27 colour management promised for this call. The sell-side bar for December is stale and flat at $373M. Management's own words in August were 'pretty confident' strength continues through 1H FY27, inbound POs 'even extending into Q2', and Q1 seasonality not expected to be significant. A December guide at or above about $380-400M against a 60-day-old $373M consensus is therefore more likely than not. The buy-side has not priced that number; it has priced a 2H FY27 cliff. Three things keep me close to 50. Peers guided the next quarter flat: ASMPT SEMI flat for Q4, BESI flat +/-5%, Amkor Q4 $1.9-2.0B against $1.99B. This is the first call for a new CEO (Talluri, from 2026-09-01), who may guide conservatively or decline to frame 2H. And in this tape, sector beat-and-raises have not been rewarded. I lean up, mainly from the stale December consensus, the depressed setup and the positive reactions this name has shown when sentiment was low. I lean up, not enough to bet on.
unpriced: The December-quarter sell-side consensus ($373.3M, $1.43) has not been revised in 60 days and is flat against a September quarter likely to come in above $375M. Management's August commentary points to flat-to-up. So a beat on the December guide against the published bar is likely. Whether the price holds it is unclear: the buy-side bar (whisper $1.61) is higher, and the 50% drawdown reflects sector-wide AI-capex fear, not KLIC data.

recommendation.reason: A beat on the December guide against a stale, flat consensus is likely, and the stock is heavily de-rated into the print. But the reaction will turn on 2H FY27 framing from a CEO on his first call, in a sector tape that has sold beat-and-raises. Peers' flat next-quarter guides also cap how strong the December number is likely to look. My edge on direction is about 60/40, below the bar to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A December-quarter revenue guide below about $370M, or a refusal to frame 2H FY27 or language about customers digesting capacity, would make this a clear down move. A guide above $400M with TCB tracking to the top of the $150-200M FY27 range would make it a strong up move.

self_critique: The strongest case for the up side: a stock -50% from its high at 11x forward EPS, a stale flat consensus and a management that beat the top of its range last quarter. Those are textbook conditions for a +10-20% relief move, like Feb 2026 (+19%) and Nov 2025 (+10.6%), so 60 may be too timid. The strongest case for the down side: the ball-bonder business just quadrupled capacity into a China build-out. Peers' flat Q4 guides hint at a pause. A new CEO has every incentive to under-promise. And the 24-point put skew says informed money wants protection. Both cases are plausible, which is why I do not recommend.
